final.memo:
Yahoo! Inc. is a premier internet media conglomerate that the market has fundamentally mispriced by failing to recognize the value of its separable Asian assets [D01]. While the company operates a massive advertising-supported platform, the equity value is currently obscured by a conglomerate discount and a history of governance failures [D01, D04].

Our sum-of-the-parts valuation reveals that the Asian stakes, combined with net cash, provide a significant floor beneath the core operating business [D01, D04]. Against internet advertising peers, the current market valuation effectively treats the core business as a decaying asset rather than an entity capable of meaningful earnings power post-restructuring [D04].

Market participants are rightfully skeptical given the board's inability to resolve the monetization of these Asian assets despite clear opportunities [D04]. The status quo is untenable; the strategic review announced on September 6, 2011, following the removal of CEO Carol Bartz, is a necessary but insufficient step toward unlocking this embedded value [D02].

We intend to engage constructively to ensure the board acts in the interest of shareholders by monetizing these Asian holdings and implementing a disciplined capital allocation strategy [D04]. Should the current board and interim leadership fail to provide a concrete, value-maximizing plan by the next annual meeting, we are prepared to launch a formal proxy contest to replace directors [D07, D04].

Our conviction is predicated on the hard floor provided by the Asian assets, which limits the downside while offering significant upside through governance-driven value realization [D01, D04]. We will monitor the strategic review process closely and are prepared to exit if the board attempts to maintain the status quo or pursues value-destructive acquisitions [D04, D07].

We are initiating a 5% position in the common stock to signal our commitment to this catalyst-driven event [D05]. We have hedged this exposure with index puts on the Nasdaq to protect against market-wide multiple compression that could impact the core advertising segment [D05].
